reasons: Lake identity verifies the case as a U.S. Supreme Court decision decided 1989-03-21 with input_case_name and record_id matching Brower v. County of Inyo.
Lake citations verify official cite 489 U.S. 593, vendor-neutral cite 1989 U.S. LEXIS 1569, and the listed parallel cites.
The opinion states that a Fourth Amendment seizure occurs only when there is a governmental termination of freedom of movement through means intentionally applied.
The opinion also states that it was enough that Brower was meant to be stopped by the physical obstacle of the roadblock and was so stopped.
residual_risks: The holding should not be read to decide reasonableness or Section 1983 liability; the Court remanded that issue.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add that the Court held the complaint sufficiently alleged a seizure and remanded the separate reasonableness issue.

reasons: The opinion describes the claim as alleging brutal, excessive, unreasonable and unnecessary physical force in establishing the roadblock.
The case involves a fatal roadblock used to stop a fleeing driver, but the page assigns only a related cross-doctrine role, not an anchor role.
residual_risks: The Court decided seizure, not ultimate excessive-force reasonableness.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep this as Related rather than Anchor for Use of Force.

The opinion concludes that the complaint sufficiently alleged respondents sought to stop Brower by roadblock and succeeded, which was enough to constitute a seizure.
